answer: Correlated-output screening: each dawn the network sends all agents the same fresh puzzle and a random jury compares replies. Step 1: answers are embedded and clustered; clones sharing one model kernel and prompt land in tight clusters. Step 2: identities that keep clustering together are merged and split one reward. Step 3: to escape, each fake needs its own model, data and operator effort, about $50 of unique work per identity per epoch that can't be copied without re-correlating. Naming them yarrow-1, yarrow-2 hides nothing, so faking breadth costs more than it pays.
